tone_statements.citation: Raymond, Timothy R. & Gerrit de Wit. 2025. Bhele grammar overview ('Grammar page', final v3, dated June 2025): nominal forms, pronominal forms, invariables, verbs. In: Bhele Dictionary (Bhele - French - Swahili - English), Webonary.org. SIL Global. 23 pp. PDF.
tone_statements.quote: In the Bhele orthography, tone is not written except in the case of minimal pairs. On this page, tone marking is added when it is known. [...] The verbal base may be simple, consisting only of a verb root, or extended, consisting of a verb root followed by one or more extensions. Extensions are underlyingly toneless. [...] In Bhele, tense in the sense of 'a point in time' is expressed by a combination of time adverbials, the final vowel and a TAM (tense/aspect/mood) tone melody on the verb form. [...] The High tone on the final vowel spreads leftward as far as the syllable following the initial syllable of the verb root.
tone_statements.locator: p. 1 (introduction) and p. 13, section 'Verbs: The structure of the verb form'

tone_statements.citation: Raymond, Timothy R. & Gerrit de Wit. 2025. Notes on Bhele phonology ('Phonology page', final v3, dated June 2025). In: Bhele Dictionary (Bhele - French - Swahili - English), Webonary.org. SIL Global. 6 pp. PDF.
tone_statements.quote: Bhele has two tone registers, High and Low. All four patterns of High and Low are attested on disyllabic noun roots. Contour tones can be seen as a combination of a Low and a High tone, linked to the same syllable. [...] Verb roots have either a High tone or a Low tone, linked to the first syllable of the root. [...] Some disyllabic High nouns are realized with a High tone on the first syllable and a lower tone (but not at the level Low) on the second. As yet it is unknown whether this is another tone level, or (non)automatic downstep. [...] Bhele has grammatical tone, i.e. verb tone melodies representing the TAM system.
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H, L; contours = L+H; possible M/downstep unresolved)

sources.note: Nothing on stress for Bhele (or Bila). Bhele appears only comparatively: 7-vowel member of the Amba-Bira-Bhele-Bila-Kaiku-Kango-Komo group (p.452); Komo/Bhele/Bila tone-marked cognate sets (pp.456-7, Bhele data from T. Raymond); p.458 'It seems plausible that Bila once had a two-tone system with downstep, like its genetically most closely related neighbors Komo and Bhele'; voiced obstruents show no tone-lowering effect in Komo and Bhele.

sources.note: Two tone registers, High and Low; all four H/L patterns attested on disyllabic noun roots; contour tones analysed as L+H on one syllable (edaa [èdâ] 'tongue', nii [nǐ] 'child'); verb roots are lexically H or L on the root-initial syllable (kéng- 'grill' vs keng- 'resemble'); some H.H nouns surface H.M and the authors leave open whether M is a third level or (non)automatic downstep; syllabic nasal prefixes carry underlying L; grammatical tone: TAM tone melodies (imperfective -a L vs infinitive -á H with leftward H spread up to but excluding the root-initial syllable), 'not yet' negative marked…
